propagation, but it cannot fully compensate for the spectral nulls because only
a part of feedback symbols is directly decided. Fortunately, maximum likelihood

eliminate the resisting spectral distortions and implement optimal detection.

can effectively suppress the burst-error propagation to obtain a maximum 2.9dB
improvement of $\boldsymbol{Q}$ factor and eliminate the phenomenon of BER
floor. In conclusion, the joint WDFE and MLSE algorithm can efficiently
compensate for the spectral nulls to obtain a maximum 3.2dB improvement of
$\boldsymbol{Q}$ factor and BER less than $1.0\times ten^{-3}$. Moreover, the
joint WDFE and MLSE algorithm can mitigate the Kapton insulation attenuation
effects to ensure the reliable data transmission between submarine platforms.

18.8km submarine optical cable to ensure the reliable data transmission between

computational energy excludes very deep TCNs, which suggests that our

variant of eigenvector centrality
for multilayer networks with inter-layer constraints on node importance.
Specifically, we consider a multilayer network defined by multiple
edge-weighted, potentially directed, graphs over the same set of nodes with
each graph representing one layer of the network and no inter-layer edges. As
in the standard eigenvector centrality construction, the importance of each
node in a given layer is based on the weighted sum of the importance of
adjacent nodes in that same layer. Unlike standard eigenvector centrality, we
assume that the adjacency relationship and the importance of adjacent nodes may
be based on distinct layers. Importantly, this type of centrality constraint is
only partially supported by existing frameworks for multilayer eigenvector
centrality that use edges between nodes in different layers to capture
inter-layer dependencies. For our model, constrained, layer-specific
eigenvector centrality values are defined by a system of independent eigenvalue
problems and dependent pseudo-eigenvalue problems, whose solution can be
efficiently realized using an interleaved power iteration algorithm.
Furthermore, the use of unconnected graph layers removes the danger of
over-emphasizing the importance of nodes that are centrally located in terms
of short-path connectivity at the expense of nodes that may be important in
terms of longer-range, hierarchical connectivity. We demonstrate the effectiveness
of our approach by applying it to (i) a set of real multilayer networks where
we see significant differences in centrality values compared to standard
eigenvector centrality, and (ii) a set of synthetic networks where we show how
our method can help to recover community structure.
  The approach presented here can be used to compute a useful variant of
multilayer eigenvector centrality and can also serve as a starting point for
the development of other multilayer network measures based on multiple, possibly
directed and weighted, but unconnected graph layers.
  We show that our method can help to recover community structure in a set of
synthetic multilayer networks.
  We study the theoretical performance of our method in terms of the narrowness
of the spectrum between nodes with high centrality and those with high degree
(Adjacency degree) and we show how to expand the approach to network systems of
interest through the use of weighted centrality.
  We study the effectiveness of our approach by applying it to a set of real
multilayer networks.

problems can be formulated as functional optimization problems with
differential equality and inequality constraints. Since these problems are
infinite-dimensional and often do not have a known analytical solution, one has
to resort to numerical methods to compute an approximate solution. This paper
uses a unifying notation to outline some of the techniques used in the
transcription step of simultaneous direct methods (which
discretize-then-optimize) for solving continuous-time dynamic optimization
problems. We focus on collocation, integrated residual and Runge-Kutta schemes.
These transcription methods are then applied to a simulation case study to
answer a question that arose during the COVID-19 pandemic, namely: If there are
not enough ventilators, is it possible to ventilate more than one patient on a
single ventilator? The results suggest that it is possible, in principle, to
estimate individual patient parameters sufficiently accurately, using a
relatively small number of flow rate measurements, without needing to
disconnect a patient from the system or needing more than one flow rate sensor.
We also show that it is possible to ensure that two different patients can
indeed receive their desired tidal volume, by modifying the resistance
experienced by the air flow to each patient and controlling the ventilator
pressure.

to be very challenging. This is due to the low contrast between the tumor and
adjacent tissues, the anatomical variation of the esophagus, as well as the
occasional presence of foreign bodies (e.g. feeding tubes). Physicians
therefore usually exploit additional knowledge such as endoscopic findings,
clinical history, additional imaging modalities like PET scans. Achieving his
additional information is time-consuming, while the results are error-prone and
might lead to non-deterministic results. In this paper we aim to investigate if
and to what extent a simplified clinical workflow based on CT alone, allows one
to automatically segment the esophageal tumor with sufficient quality. For this
purpose, we present a fully automatic end-to-end esophageal tumor segmentation
method based on convolutional neural networks (CNNs). The proposed network,
called Dilated Dense Attention Unet (DDAUnet), leverages spatial and channel
attention gates in each dense block to selectively concentrate on determinant
feature maps and regions. Dilated convolutional layers are used to manage GPU
memory and increase the network receptive field. We collected a dataset of 792
scans from 288 distinct patients including varying anatomies with \mbox{air

with a mean intersection over union of 0.763. Compared to existing methods,

simpler to train and to interpret, as it does not require complicated deformation
models and registration processes. Furthermore, with a depth of only 23

extraction techniques, named entity recognition (NER) is widely used to extract
information from texts for downstream tasks. Nested NER is a branch of NER in
which the named entities (NEs) are nested with each other. However, most of the
previous studies on nested NER usually apply linear structure to model the
nested NEs which are actually accommodated in a hierarchical structure. Thus in
order to address this mismatch, this work models the full nested NEs in a
sentence as a holistic structure, then we propose a holistic structure parsing
algorithm to disclose the entire NEs once for all. Besides, there is no
research on applying corpus-level information to NER currently. To make up for
the loss of this information, we introduce Point-wise Mutual Information (PMI)
and other frequency features from corpus-aware statistics for even better
performance by holistic modeling from sentence-level to corpus-level.
Experiments show that our model yields promising results on widely-used
benchmarks which approach or even achieve state-of-the-art. Further empirical
studies show that our proposed corpus-aware features can substantially improve
NER domain adaptation, which demonstrates the surprising advantage of our
proposed corpus-level holistic structure modeling.

also to get a more reliable score. Finally, we can use self-supervised
evaluation methods, where we look at how well a system can recognize
information from the caption back in the image.

a major barrier in kidney
transplantation (KT). The increasing shortage of kidney donors has driven the
development of desensitization techniques to overcome this immunological
challenge. Compared with compatible KT, patients undergoing incompatible KTs
are more likely to experience rejection, infection, malignancy, and graft loss.
We study the optimal acceptance of possibly incompatible kidneys for individual
end-stage kidney disease patients. To capture the effect of incompatibility, we
propose a Markov Decision Process (MDP) model that explicitly includes
compatibility as a state variable. The resulting higher-dimensional model makes
it more challenging to analyze, but under suitable conditions, we derive
structural properties including control limit-type optimal policies that are
easy to compute and implement. Numerical examples illustrate the behavior of
the optimal policy under different mismatch levels and highlight the importance
of explicitly incorporating the incompatibility level into the acceptance
decision when desensitization therapy is an option.
  We also validate the model's predictions against real-world data from the
United States Scientific Registry of Transplant Recipients (SRTR). Our approach
offers a tool for evaluating and comparing immunological outcomes of KTs when
incompatibility is a primary concern. Finally, this tool can be used to help
guide individual patient care by providing a rigorous framework for evaluating
the trade-off between the potential benefits of accepting a incompatible kidney
and the risks of rejection and other adverse outcomes.

criteria, desensitization, compatibility, mismatch level, real-world data

high dimensions. This broad class of copulas is introduced and surveyed,
including elliptical copulas, skew $t$ copulas, factor copulas, time series
copulas and regression copulas. The common auxiliary representation of implicit
copulas is outlined, and how this makes them both scalable and tractable for
statistical modeling. Issues such as parameter identification, extended
likelihoods for discrete or mixed data, parsimony in high dimensions, and
simulation from the copula model are considered. Bayesian approaches to
estimate the copula parameters, and predict from an implicit copula model, are
outlined. Particular attention is given to implicit copula processes

of current research. Two econometric applications -- one from macroeconomic
time series and the other from financial asset pricing -- illustrate the

nonlinear relationships between variables, and do so in high dimensions with a
tractable joint distribution. We show that the step of selecting the
variables to include in the regression can be regarded as a partitioning
problem, with the objective function being the log-likelihood, and solve it
using a new algorithm that only requires backcasting (predicting backwards in
time) from the selected variables. In a macroeconomic application, this
approach is shown to outperform the standard selection methods in terms of
forecast accuracy and model fit. Keywords: implicit copula, regression
copula, Bayesian statistics, macroeconometrics, financial time series.

banks. The Central Bank Forecast Regression Copula (CBFRC) is a statistical
model that describes the joint distribution of multiple forecasts from a single
perspective. The framework is applicable to any multi-forecast setting and has
the considerable advantage of allowing for heterogeneity in forecasting
accuracy. We show that the advantage of using the CBFRC over other popular
methods is evident in forecasting out-of-sample inflation rates, with the CBFRC
outperforming the alternative methods considered in this study. A case study
comparing forecast accuracy in five high-income countries is presented, and
we find that the CBFRC is able to improve on the Bank's own method in three out
of five countries. A case study comparing density forecast accuracy is also

currently used in computational
linguistics rely on unary modalities to allow for the controlled application of
structural rules affecting word order and phrase structure. These controlled
structural operations give rise to derivational ambiguities that are missed by
the original Lambek Calculus or its pregroup simplification. Proposals for
compositional interpretation of extended Lambek Calculus in the compact closed
category of FVect and linear maps have been made, but in these proposals the
syntax-semantics mapping ignores the control modalities, effectively
restricting their role to the syntax. Our aim is to turn the modalities into
first-class citizens of the vectorial interpretation. Building on the
directional density matrix semantics, we extend the interpretation of the type
system with an extra spin density matrix space. The interpretation of proofs
then results in ambiguous derivations being tensored with orthogonal spin
states. Our method introduces a way of simultaneously representing co-existing
interpretations of ambiguous utterances, and provides a uniform framework for
the integration of lexical and derivational ambiguity.
  We achieve this extended interpretation by adding four new valuation
functions, which assign density matrices to types and proofs. We show how the
new valuations for proofs incorporate the co-iteration axioms of the vector
logic and how they allow for the representation of multiple interpretations,
given ambiguity. Finally, we show how our method extends to types with modal
operators.
  Our approach leads to a way of representing co-existing interpretations of
ambiguous utterances, which is crucial in dialogue modelling, where mis-
understandings can exploit contextual information to disambiguate utterances.
Moreover, by extending the type system with controlled structural operations,
we can generate a wide range of ambiguous derivations. As a result, we provide
a uniform framework for integrating derivational and lexical ambiguity.
Lastly, we lead the reader through an example of how we can use our framework
in the modelling of sentence semantics.
  Keywords: extended Lambek Calculus, modalities, ambiguity, density matrix
semantics, linear logic, type theory.

subsequently use correlated actions as in the standard model of correlated

the correlated metallic state of LaNiO$_3$ in a series of LaNiO$_3$/LaAlO$_3$
superlattices as a function of bilayer thickness. Spin-lattice relaxation
measurements in an applied field of 6.55 T reveal two equal amplitude
components: one with metallic ($T$-linear) $1/T_{1}$, and a second with a more
complex $T$-dependence. The metallic character of the slow relaxing component

much more sensitive, exhibiting the opposite temperature dependence (increasing
towards low $T$) in the thinnest, most magnetic samples. The origin of this
bipartite relaxation is discussed.
  We propose that the fast relaxing component reflects spin correlations on the
"outer" NiO$_2$ planes that are inconsistent with the long-range, neutron-determined
antiferromagnetic ordering of the bulk LaNiO$_3$. That these outer-plane
correlations are more sensitive to the thickness of the LaNiO$_3$ layer than
inferred from neutron studies of the average structure point towards a
non-uniform, possibly charge or spin ordering, in these superlattices.
Ultimately, the outer-plane correlations are responsible for the low $T$
metal-insulator transition in the thinnest LaNiO$_3$ / LaAlO$_3$ superlattices.
Finally, we propose that by choosing appropriate thicknesses, it may be possible
to isolate the isolated slow relaxing component in a zero field measurement,
providing an unprecedented look at the zero field spin lattice relaxation of

propose a simple scoring algorithm, based on bipartite graph matching, to
optimally incorporate a set of diverse references. We study multiple language
generation tasks at different levels of predictive conversation depth, using
textual attributes induced automatically from pretrained classifiers. Our
culminating task is a challenging theory of mind problem, a controllable
generation task which requires reasoning about the expected reaction of the
listener.

designing primarily for diversity, and we find that improving diversity
significantly requires a high branching factor. We further analyze how attributes
induced from pretrained classifiers can be used to improve the quality of the
diverse set of references, and we find significant benefits for all of our tasks
when using attributes to continue the conversation in a more age-appropriate
style.

continuation algorithm which selectively continues a branch by a human annotator,
and we find that this can be used to improve the diversity of generations
significantly while maintaining quality only modestly slightly worse than
traditional data balancing approaches.

looked at this problem from a linguistic perspective, in this paper we take a
more mechanical view and investigate different scoring metrics used to evaluate
a diverse set of generations, finding that some may seriously suboptimal
performances (especially in the high branching setting), and others are
surprisingly optimal.

theoretical knowledge about the domain into the diverse set of references,

intelligent reflecting surface (IRS). In addition, we account for the effects
of correlated Rayleigh fading and the intertwinement between the amplitude and
the phase shift of the reflecting coefficient of each IRS element, which are
usually both neglected despite their presence in practice. Random matrix theory
tools allow to derive the probability density function (PDF) of the cascaded
channel in closed form, and subsequently, the EC, which depend only on the
large-scale statistics and the phase shifts. Notably, we optimize the EC with
respect to the phase shifts with low overhead, i.e., once per several coherence
intervals instead of the burden of frequent necessary optimization required by
expressions being dependent on instantaneous channel information. Monte-Carlo
(MC) simulations verify the analytical results and demonstrate the insightful
interplay among the key parameters and their impact on the EC.

system and derive the sum-EC, which depends on the linear beamforming vectors.

phase shifts, with no overhead except for the frequent optimization of the
beamforming which can be done recursively with little extra expense. Once again,
the analytical results are verified by MC simulations, and show that by simply
optimizing the phase shifts we can gain significant amounts of sum-EC, as
compared to a system which uses only beamforming.

beamforming vectors and power allocation, with a special emphasis on the power
allocation problem being solved efficiently with low overhead. Closed-form
expressions for the maximum SNR achievable by any combination of power allocation

channel model are introduced. Section III derives the EC of a P2P MIMO system

extended-Hubbard and XXZ spin
models result in dynamically-bound clusters at neighboring sites. We show that
the dynamics of these clusters in two-dimensional lattices is remarkably
different and richer than that of repulsively-bound on-site clusters in gases
without inter-site interactions. Whereas on-site pairs move in the same lattice
as individual particles, nearest-neighbor dimers perform an interacting quantum
walk in a different lattice geometry, leading to a peculiar dynamics
characterized by more than one time scale. The latter is general for any
lattice geometry, but it is especially relevant in triangular and diamond
lattices, where dimers move resonantly in an effective kagome and Lieb lattice,
respectively. As a result, dimers experience partial quasi-localization due to
an effective flat band, and may move slower than longer clusters. This
surprising link between anomalously slow quantum walk dynamics in these models
and flat-band physics may be readily observed in experiments with lanthanide
atoms.
  We also show that spin dimers in the XXZ model map onto hard-core bosons
interacting in a certain pairwise-dependent way. This mapping is particularly
useful for studying spin dynamics in these models, as it eliminates spin
symmetries and allows for the investigation of quantum many-body dynamics
using a plethora of tools developed for interacting bosons.
  Finally, we reveal that up to a certain interaction strength, spin dimers in
the XXZ model and extended-Hubbard model behave differently. In particular, the
flat band associated with the quantum walk of these dimers leads to macroscopically
coherent states in the spin system, as well as instability towards the
formation of more complicated cluster states. We identify two interaction
regimes with peculiar physics: a low-interaction regime where these cluster
states are stable, and a strong-interaction regime where they decay to more
simple coherent states. This is no doubt fascinating, as cluster states are a
fundamental resource for quantum computation, and can be generated from any
coherent state.
  This work is a fundamental basis for further investigations of dynamically
bound clusters in lasers and disordered potentials, as well as cluster state
dynamics and quantum computing.

drawing, where each set of objects is visualized as a set of vertices (points)
on one of the two parallel horizontal lines and the relationships are
represented by edges (simple curves) between the two lines connecting the
corresponding vertices. One of the common objectives in such drawings is to
minimize the number of crossings this, however, is computationally expensive
and may still result in drawings with so many crossings that they affect the
readability of the drawing. We consider a recent approach to remove crossings
in such visualizations by splitting vertices, where the goal is to find the
minimum number of vertices to be split to obtain a planar drawing. We show that
determining whether a planar drawing exists after splitting at most $k$
vertices is fixed parameter tractable in $k$.
  Furthermore, we get parameterized complexity results for the problem where
the number of splits $k$ is restricted to a set of possible values. Our
approaches use recent fixed parameter tractability results for the general
problem when restricted to linear drawings, and deterministically find
planar drawings with at most two vertex splits for these cases. We also
construct an example to show that the fixed parameter tractability of the
general case cannot be extended to three vertex splits. Finally, we determine
the exact value of the smallest number of vertex splits required to make the
graph of Facebook users - which is a bipartite graph itself, planar.

bipartite. Here, we get a tractable algorithm for finding the minimum number of
vertices to be split if the number of splits $k$ is at least as large as the
number of crossings in the original drawing, and a quasi-polynomial
algorithm for $k=\Omega(n^2)$, where $n$ is the number of vertices. For the
general case we give a XP algorithm for the case when $k=n$. For $k=o(n)$
we give a first deterministic algorithm for this case, however its running time
is not practical. We also determine the exact value of the smallest number of
vertex splits required to make the graph planar for many social network
datasets, including the graph of movie actors, which is not bipartite.

multiple parities to jointly train a powerful machine learning model without
sharing their private data. According to the form of collaboration, FL can be
further divided into horizontal federated learning (HFL) and vertical federated
learning (VFL). In HFL, participants share the same feature space and
collaborate on data samples, while in VFL, participants share the same sample
IDs and collaborate on features. VFL has a broader scope of applications and is
arguably more suitable for joint model training between large enterprises.
  In this paper, we focus on VFL and investigate potential privacy leakage in
real-world VFL frameworks. We design and implement two practical privacy
attacks: reverse multiplication attack for the logistic regression VFL
protocol; and reverse sum attack for the XGBoost VFL protocol. We empirically
show that the two attacks are (1) effective - the adversary can successfully
steal the private training data, even when the intermediate outputs are
encrypted to protect data privacy; (2) evasive - the attacks do not deviate
from the protocol specification nor deteriorate the accuracy of the target
model; and (3) easy - the adversary needs little prior knowledge about the data
distribution of the target participant. We also show the leaked information is
as effective as the raw training data in training an alternative classifier. We
further show that the logitic regression and XGBoost protocols leak different
information even with the same VFL framework. We highlight the origin of the
leakage, and propose protocols with theoretical guarantee of privacy leakage
in FL. We argue that practical privacy leakage assessment of VFL is crucial,
and is left to future work.

features. While this method proved very popular, still it exists shortcomings
to be effectively used. As RFF samples the randomized features from a
distribution independent of training data, it requires sufficient large number
of feature expansions to have similar performances to kernelized classifiers,
and this is proportional to the number samples in the dataset. Thus, reducing
the number of feature dimensions is necessary to effectively scale to large
datasets. In this paper, we propose a kernel approximation method in a data
dependent way, coined as Pseudo Random Fourier Features (PRFF) for reducing the
number of feature dimensions and also to improve the prediction performance.
The proposed approach is evaluated on classification and regression problems
and compared with the RFF, orthogonal random features and Nystr{\"o}m approach
over synthetic and real datasets.
  We investigate the performance of Random Fourier Features (RFF) in kernel
method and show that it is suboptimal. We propose Pseudo Random Fourier Features
(PRFF) to improve the performance of RFF. PRFF is a deterministic approach to
generate the Fourier features (along feature dimensions much less than the
data size) using training data itself for improving the prediction performance
beyond RFF. We compare RFF and PRFF in classification and regression scenarios
over synthetic and real datasets. PrFF is observed to outperform RFF in terms
of prediction performance and also by reducing the number of feature dimensions
considerably than RFF.

surgery in patients with the congenital heart disease Tetralogy of Fallot (TOF)
is mainly based on ventricular volume and function according to current
guidelines. Both of these two biomarkers are most reliably assessed by
segmentation of 3D cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) images. In several grand
challenges in the last years, U-Net architectures have shown impressive results
on the provided data. However, in clinical practice, data sets are more diverse
considering individual pathologies and image properties derived from different
scanner properties. Additionally, specific training data for complex rare
diseases like TOF is scarce.
  For this work, 1) we assessed the accuracy gap when using a publicly
available labelled data set (the Automatic Cardiac Diagnosis Challenge (ACDC)
data set) for training and subsequent applying it to CMR data of TOF patients
and vice versa and 2) whether we can achieve similar results when applying the
model to a more heterogeneous data base.
  Multiple deep learning models were trained with four-fold cross validation.
Afterwards they were evaluated on the respective unseen CMR images from the
other collection. Our results confirm that current deep learning models can
achieve excellent results (left ventricle dice of
$0.951\pm{0.003}$/$0.941\pm{0.007}$ train/validation) however with a
significant reduction of quality when applied to a new data base (dice of
$0.826\pm{0.012}$/$0.817\pm{0.010}$ validation/train). This is specifically
visible when the CMR images are resampled to a lower isotropic resolution
during the evaluation phase. Using the ACDC data for training and subsequent
applying it to CMR data of TOF patients yields excellent results above the
guidelines requirements. We show that also CMR images from TOF patients can be
properly segmented when enough general information is learned during training.
The presented work highlights the potential as well as the pitfalls of deep
learning based ventricle segmentation when using CMR images from different
patient groups.

insights on how deep learning based segmentations can be used to support the
clinical planning process of TOF patients.

transfer (SWIPT) is presented as a means of not only helping to communicate and
access information with increasing efficiency in the next generation of mobile
data networks but also contributing to minimizing a network's overall power
consumption by providing a green energy source. First, a unique architecture is
proposed that harvests energy from an access point (AP) without the receiver
needing a splitter. In the proposed system model, a portion of the spectrum is
used for information decoding (ID) while the remaining portion is exploited for
energy harvesting (EH) in an orthogonal frequency division multiple access
(OFDMA) network. To investigate the performance gain, an optimization problem
is formulated that maximizes the harvested energy of a multi-user single-cell
OFDMA downlink (DL) network with SWIPT and also satisfies a minimum data-rate
requirement for all users. A locally optimal solution for the underlying
problem, which is essentially non-convex due to the coupling of the integer
variable, is obtained by using optimization tools. Second, the proposed system
model is improved in order to investigate the resource allocation problem of
needing to maximize throughput based on the separated receiver architecture in
an OFDMA multi-user multi-cell system that uses SWIPT. The resulting problem,
which jointly optimizes the subcarrier assignment and power allocation, is a
mixed-integer non-linear problem (MINLP), and, due to its complexity, needs a
decoupled solution strategy. Finally, a set of optimal subcarrier assignments
and power allocations are obtained through a novel coupling scheme, which
assures global optimality. Numerical results show that the overall throughput
is greater than the case where neithersubcarrier assignments nor power allocations
are optimized, and also that the largest gain (around 200%) is achieved in an
actual network scenario compared to a separate architecture with no splitter.
Results also show that the gain achieved by optimizing power in a joint fashion
is around 55%, and that the gain achieved by optimizing subcarrier assignments
is around 40%.
  The proposed idea of joint subcarrier and power optimization for multi-user
single-cell OFDMA downlink network that uses SWIPT achieves a significant
increase in harvested energy compared to the existing schemes. The overall
design of a system that uses SWIPT introduces new architectural possibilities
and alternatives for improving the performance of future wireless networks.

integrating FPN. It makes each level of the backbone network only has the

analysis, two feasible strategies are proposed to enable each level of the
backbone to look at all objects in the FPN-based detection frameworks.
Specifically, one is to introduce auxiliary objective functions to make each
backbone level directly receive the back-propagation signals of various-scale
objects during training. The other is to construct the feature pyramid in a
more reasonable way to avoid the irrational back-propagation paths. Extensive
experiments on the COCO benchmark validate the soundness of our analysis and
the effectiveness of our methods. Without bells and whistles, we demonstrate
that our method achieves solid improvements (more than 2%) on various detection
frameworks: one-stage, two-stage, anchor-based, anchor-free and

language, words of the same form can take different meanings depending on
context. While humans easily infer the meaning or gloss of such words by their
context, machines stumble on this task.As such, we intend to replicated and
expand upon the results of Huang et al.GlossBERT, a model which they design to
disambiguate these words (Huang et al.,2019). Specifically, we propose the
following augmentations: data-set tweaking(alpha hyper-parameter), ensemble
methods, and replacement of BERT with BART andALBERT. The following GitHub
repository contains all code used in this report, which extends on the code
made available by Huang et al.
  We achieve significant gains over the baseline model, to which we make a
number of adjustments to boost performance. We see an increase in F-score of
0.41 over the baseline model on the full dataset, and an increase of 2.35 on
the difficult dataset.
  We also see that we achieve the best results when performing a
transformed-disambiguation task, rather than the standard disambiguation task
as is common in previous work. That is, we find that we achieve higher scores
on the disambiguation task when mapping 10 senses to 10 senses, than when
mapping 10 senses to 1 sense.
  Finally, we see that we achieve the best results when using BART as the TSD
model, surpassing both BERT and ALBERT by 0.39 and 0.30 respectively in F-score
on the full dataset.
  On the whole, we see that a number of adjustments including data-set tweaking
and ensemble methods, as well as model augmentation with BART, all contribute
to an increase in performance on the WSD task.
  By extending on the work of Huang et al.(2019), we hope to make a number of
contributions to the WSD literature, and explore a number of open questions in
the field.
  We begin by introducing the WSD task in Section 1. In Section 2, we
introduce the model of Huang et al.(2019), which we will be extending and
augmenting. We describe both the micro and macro data-adjustment experiments
in Section 3, as well as the ensemble experiments in Section 4. Finally, we
describe the model-adjustment experiments in Section 5.

and reason about real world task procedures, which often requires thorough
understanding of temporal common sense and multimodal information, as these
procedures are often communicated through a combination of texts and images.
Such capability is essential for applications such as sequential task planning
and multi-source instruction summarization. While humans are capable of
reasoning about and sequencing unordered multimodal procedural instructions,
whether current machine learning models have such essential capability is still
an open question. In this work, we benchmark models' capability of reasoning
over and sequencing unordered multimodal instructions by curating datasets from
popular online instructional manuals and collecting comprehensive human
annotations. We find models not only perform significantly worse than humans
but also seem incapable of efficiently utilizing the multimodal information. To
improve machines' performance on multimodal event sequencing, we propose
sequentiality-aware pretraining techniques that exploit the sequential
alignment properties of both texts and images, resulting in > 5% significant
improvements.
  Our findings demonstrate the importance of curriculum learning for efficient
evaluation during testing and validate the effectiveness of the proposed
sequentiality-aware pretraining methods. We also propose a comprehensive
evaluation framework that considers not only exact sequentiality but also
logical and topological reorderings, which is essential for evaluating models'
capability of reasoning over and sequencing unordered multimodal instructions.
This framework leads to more comprehensive and rigorous results.
  Ultimately, our work highlights the importance of accounting for unordered
information and sequentiality in multimodal language understanding and
summarization.

in developing strategies of
eradicating spreads of malicious phenomena in networks, such as epidemics and
fake information, which are generally named in the research networks
immunization. The traditional approach of evaluating the effectiveness of
attacks on networks, is focused on measuring some macro parameters related to
an entire attack, such as the critical probability of a percolation occurrence
in the network $p_c$ and the relative size of the largest component in the
network - the giant component, but not considering the attack on a micro
perspective, which is the analysis of the node removals, during an attack,
themselves, their characteristics and results. In this paper we present and
apply the last method of focusing on the micro scale of an attack. Based on the
theory of percolation in networks, we analyze the phenomenon of an avalanche
results due to a single node removal from a network, that is a state in which a
removal of one node belongs to the network's giant component causes other nodes
to be also disconnected from it, which is a much greater contribution to the
fragmentation (immunization) of the network than only the single original node
removal itself. Specifically, we focus ourselves on the parameter of the size
of an avalanche, which is the number of nodes that are disconnected from the
giant component due to a single node removal. Relating to a node removal
microscopic description, one network can produce different results onto an
avalance, depending on its structure, thus getting a picture of an attack on
the network microscopically. This approach is useful for analyzing the spread of
malicious phenomena in networks, which are generally studied through
simulations of real networks, which are too much specific, in order to contribute
to the general understanding of the matter. Furthermore, the concept of an
avalance is not considered in the study of percolation in networks, which is
important from the point of view of the associated uncertainty structure, as
indicated by the variety of microscopic states that can be encountered in a
network. It is also noteworthy that the idea of an avalanche is not a new one,
as it is known in the context of electrical networks (circuits) as a characteristic
feature of stable operation, but in the context of networks in general, the
concept is new and useful.

gravitational waves from the binary neutron star mergers in the current and the
future generation detectors, as it does not depend on either the arm length, or
the injected squeezing level. In this paper, we come up with the sloshing
Sagnac interferometer topology, which can be obtained from the Michelson
interferometer by optically connecting the end mirrors into an additional
optical cavity. This transforms the interferometer into a triply-coupled cavity
system capable of beating the loss-induced high-frequency limit of the
signal-recycled Michelson interferometer. With advanced LIGO+ comparable
parameters, a sloshing-Sagnac scheme can achieve 7 times better sensitivity at
2.5\,kHz or 4 times better signal to noise ratio for a typical waveform of
binary neutron post merge. Being an evolution of Michelson interferometer, the
sloshing-Sagnac interferometer can possibly be used as a topology for the
future generation detectors and upgrade of current detectors.
  By properly tuning the oscillation mode in the sloshing Sagnac interferometer
it is possible to beat the loss-induced limit up to 4\,kHz, thus expanding the
detectability of binary neutron post merges, but an proper optimization of the
parameters is required.
  Finally, we show that also a system with just two coupled cavities is able to
be free from the loss-induced limit, thus validating the intuition that the
three coupled cavities are not strictly necessary. This simplification can be
useful for the design of future detectors.

multiple-output (XL-MIMO)
systems are seen as a promising technology for providing very high data rates
in increased user-density scenarios. Spatial non-stationarities and visibility
regions (VRs) appear across the XL-MIMO array since its large dimension is of
the same order as the distances to the user-equipments (UEs). Due to the
increased density of UEs in typical applications of XL-MIMO systems and the
scarcity of pilots, the design of random access (RA) protocols and scheduling
algorithms become challenging. In this paper, we propose a joint RA and
scheduling protocol, namely non-overlapping VR XL- MIMO (NOVR-XL) RA protocol,
which takes advantage of the different VRs of the UEs for improving RA
performance, besides seeking UEs with non-overlapping VRs to be scheduled in
the same payload data pilot resource. Our results reveal that the proposed
scheme achieves significant gains in terms of sum rate compared with
traditional RA schemes, as well as reducing access latency and improving
connectivity performance as a whole.

of disks surrounding young stars have shown that their morphology is made of
azimuthally-symmetric or point-symmetric substructures, in some cases with

from high-resolution 3D radiative hydrodynamical models which follow the
evolution of gas and solids in a protoplanetary disk. We focus on substructures
in the distribution of millimeter-sized and smaller solid particles produced by
the vertical shear instability. We show that their characteristics are
compatible with some of the shallow gaps detected in recent observations at

better sensitivity and angular resolution with ALMA and a Next Generation Very

pressure inside with respect to the outside reference space so that microbes

stealthy attack on NPRs by spoofing a DPS at its resonant frequency. Our
contributions are: (1) We show that DPSs used in NPRs typically have resonant
frequencies in the audible range. (2) We use this finding to design malicious
music to create resonance in DPSs, resulting in an overshooting in the DPS's
normal pressure readings. (3) We show how the resonance in DPSs can fool the
BMSs so that the NPR turns its negative pressure to a positive one, causing a
potential \textit{leak} of deadly microbes from NPRs. We do experiments on 8
DPSs from 5 different manufacturers to evaluate their resonant frequencies
considering the sampling tube length and find resonance in 6 DPSs. We can
achieve a 2.5 Pa change in negative pressure from a DPS that is monitoring a

of a BSL-1 lab.

of firming in low-carbon grids. A
common concern raised from ex-post assessments is that storage resources can
fail to respond to strong price signals during times of scarcity. While
commonly attributed to forecast error or failures in operations, we posit that
this behavior can be explained from the perspective of risk-averse scheduling.
Using a stochastic self-scheduling framework and real-world data harvested from
the Australian National Electricity Market, we demonstrate that risk-averse
storage resources tend to have a myopic operational perspective, that is, they
typically engage in near-term price arbitrage and chase only few extreme price
spikes and troughs, thus remaining idle in several time periods with markedly
high and low prices. This has important policy implications given the
non-transparency of unit risk aversion and apparent risk in intervention
decision-making.
  We show that transparency in risk aversion can be achieved by using tools
developed in modern risk management. Most importantly, these approaches allow
to measure the contribution of forecast error and scarcity along the risk
frontier, thus providing risk-adjusted metrics to evaluate storage resource
performance. This is not possible using traditional risk-neutral performance
metrics. Our results highlight the importance of considering the risk
perspective when assessing storage resources - and possibly other resources as
well - to avoid drawing risk-averse behavior to risk.
  Finally, we show that robust scheduling provides a transparent alternative
solution for storing risk along the uncertainty set, thus providing a boundary
on the worst possible prices that the resource can face. This allows the
resource to optimize directly under uncertainty without having to take explicit
risk attitudes.
  The novel metrics and approaches provided in this work provide an essential
toolkit for ex-ante assessment and ranking of storage resources as well as
establish a framework for evaluating the performance of storage resources as
part of larger low-carbon grids.
  We also propose the notion of a "storage portfolio" to describe a collection
of storage resources with varying risk aversion and uncertainty attitudes. The
portfolio can be optimized directly over the uncertainty set using robust
scheduling, thus providing a mechanism to manage risk and uncertainty over
operations. This provides a premium to resources that can take on more risk and
attains a diversity of perspectives over risk and uncertainty, thus leading to
more flexible and risk-aware scheduling decisions.
  Finally, we show that beyond storage, the approach presented in this work can
be applied to assess and rank resources based on their operational risk
attitudes

learning model trust score; (2) filter the top and bottom $K$ ranked instances
based on a human rule-based procedure considered safe; (3) get human labels
for the middle ranked instances that are likely to be improved with few additional
labels; (4) apply geometric data augmentation and rerun the learned model on

\section{Introduction}

In \cite{Gut} M. Gutperle proposes a conjecture for the volume of a
non-perturbative, generic, static, 3-dimensional (spacetime) shape (called a
\emph{foam}) in terms of an invariant of its (multiple) closed, non-intersecting
virtual loops. Virtual loops are allowed to pass through each other. The
invariant is a generalization of the colored Jones polynomial. Gutperle's
conjecture motivates the definition of $J_n^T$, the toroidal colored Jones
polynomial. $J_n^T$ agrees with Gutperle's proposed invariant on a particular
class of foams called \emph{torus foams}. We prove that $J_n^T$ satisfies the
volume conjecture for the 2-by-2 square weave, and give computational evidence for
other links.

of differential privacy (DP) in the
context of graph-structured data. We discuss the formulations of DP applicable
to the publication of graphs and their associated statistics as well as machine
learning on graph-based data, including graph neural networks (GNNs). The
formulation of DP in the context of graph-structured data is difficult, as
individual data points are interconnected (often non-linearly or sparsely).
This connectivity complicates the computation of individual privacy loss in
differentially private learning. The problem is exacerbated by an absence of a
single, well-established formulation of DP in graph settings. This issue
extends to the domain of GNNs, rendering private machine learning on
graph-structured data a challenging task. A lack of prior systematisation work
motivated us to study graph-based learning from a privacy perspective. In this
work, we systematise different formulations of DP on graphs, discuss challenges
and promising applications, including the GNN domain. We compare and separate
works into graph analysis tasks and graph learning tasks with GNNs. Finally, we
conclude our work with a discussion of open questions and potential directions
for further research in this area.

DP to guarantee that the published graph is private with respect to the
underlying true graph. Unlike prior approaches, our algorithm does not rely on
the use of a proxy distribution and the resulting issues of sample efficiency

reconstructed by a powerful adversary. However, the guarantee of privacy for

simulating the otherwise difficult-to-compute dynamics of quantum many-body
systems. In this work we derive, within the positive-P phase-space formalism, a
new stochastic hydrodynamic method for the description of interacting Bose
gases. It goes beyond existing hydrodynamic approaches, such as superfluid
hydrodynamics or generalized hydrodynamics, in its capacity to simulate the
full quantum dynamics of these systems: it possesses the ability to compute
non-equilibrium quantum correlations, even for short-wavelength phenomena.
Using this description, we derive a linearized stochastic hydrodynamic scheme
which is able to simulate such non-equilibrium situations for longer times than
the full positive-P approach, at the expense of approximating the treatment of
quantum fluctuations, and show that this linearized scheme can be directly
connected with existing Bogoliubov approaches. Furthermore, we go on to
demonstrate the usefulness and advantages of this formalism by exploring the
correlations that arise in a quantum shock wave scenario and comparing its
predictions to other established quantum many-body approaches.
  We find that the full positive-P approach is able to capture the onset of
condensation in a shrinking wave packet, while the linearized scheme is able to
describe the formation of a quantum shock wave, a region of rapidly changing
phase and amplitude, which is consistent with experimental observations.
Additionally, we show that the issue of odd-number symmetry in the shock wave
scenario can be explained by the atoms occupying odd-numbered sites only. This
provides a simple, intuitive understanding of the problem, which has been
observed in several experimental setups.
  Finally, we propose a direct connection between the full positive-P approach
and recent experimental implementations in opto-mechanical systems. This could
assist in the further development and implementation of quantum hydrodynamics
in laboratory settings.
  We hope that this work will contribute to further developments and implementations of
the positive-P formalism and its connections to experiment.

observed in the edge plasma of the JET tokamak. Although PTMs are well
documented, little is known about the mechanisms which produce these
structures. In the case of the PTM, an ELM-postcursor, its genesis is usually
explained by ergodisation of the magnetic field due to edge localized modes and
the appearance of a seed magnetic island which evolves into a PTM later. In
this study we try to invoke a creation mechanism based on the concepts and
observations in edge plasma turbulence. An interesting aspect of plasma
turbulence is the occurrence of coherent, long-lived structures in the
scrape-off-layer (SOL). These localized and magnetic-field-aligned regions with
higher or lower plasma densities are called blobs and holes. Measurements show
that these filaments carry parallel currents. We thus here interpret
ELM-filaments as massive blobs and the interspace between these filaments as
holes. We demonstrate that a forward-modelled closed current filament on a q=3
surface produces similar magnetic fluctuations as measured by the JET in-vessel
magnetic pickup coils if a PTM is present. From that we deduce that if a hole
is captured on a q=3 surface after an ELM-crash, a PTM equivalent signature is
generated. If the ELM-filament itself is captured on a q=3 surface, a
temporary PTM-like signature is produced. From comparisons of measurements with
numerical simulations it is evident that the ELM-filament can be considered
as a massive blob and the formation of the PTM can be described by the
interaction of multiple filaments.

concept of plasma turbulence can be applied to edge plasma phenomena. While
this study focuses on the specific PTM mode, our approach offers a general
perspective on the interaction between turbulent plasma filaments and the
magnetic field geometry.
  Finally, understanding the origin of these localized, long-lived structures
may contribute to the resolution of the mystery of their sources and sinks,
i.e., their complete formation and dissipation.

LDP (large deviation principle) for the empirical process of words, the rate
function is the specific relative entropy of the observed law of words w.r.t.\
the reference law of words. In Birkner, Greven and den Hollander \cite{BGdH10}
the \emph{quenched} LDP (= conditional on a typical letter sequence) was
derived for the case where the renewal times have an \emph{algebraic} tail. The
rate function turned out to be a sum of two terms, one being the annealed rate
function, the other being proportional to the specific relative entropy of the
observed law of letters w.r.t.\ the reference law of letters, obtained by
concatenating the words and randomising the location of the origin. The
proportionality constant equals the tail exponent of the renewal process.
  The purpose of the present paper is to extend both LDP's to letter sequences
that are not i.i.d. It is shown that both LDP's carry over when the letter
sequence satisfies a mixing condition called \emph{summable variation}. The
rate functions are again given by specific relative entropies w.r.t.\ the
reference law of words (annealed) or words plus letters (quenched). The
variation condition makes the LDP's valid under stronger convergence results
than the i.i.d.\ assumption. The conditional LDP allows one to prove a
convergence result of the form $\mathbb{P}( \frac{1}{N} \sum_w \phi(w) \to
\inf_{\mu^*} (\phi+\hat{\beta}\mu^*) ) \thicksim e^{N \hat{\beta}}$, where $\phi$
is a regular function, $\hat{\beta}$ is the rate function, $\mu^*$ the
equilibrium measure, when $N \to \infty$. The main novelty is that $\hat{\beta$
is not a function of the observed law of words alone, but also of the law of
letters, even when considering the quenched LDP. This leads to LDP's that are
useful for higher-level functions than just homogeneous functions.

optimized and non-optimized IRS scenarios. Numerical simulations indicate that
the IRS can enhance the target parameter estimation when the LOS link is weaker
than $\sim 10^{-1}$ in relative strength in comparison with the NLOS link.

optimization is not feasible, thus indicating robustness of such a solution.
These results demonstrate the potential of IRS in improving the moving target

considerable progress in this area in the past years, measuring and comparing
the effectiveness of fuzzers is still an open research question. In software
testing, the gold standard for evaluating test quality is mutation analysis,
assessing the ability of a test to detect synthetic bugs; if a set of tests
fails to detect such mutations, it will also fail to detect real bugs. Mutation
analysis subsumes various coverage measures and provides a large and diverse
set of faults that can be arbitrarily hard to trigger and detect, thus
preventing the problems of saturation and overfitting. Unfortunately, the cost
of traditional mutation analysis is exorbitant for fuzzing, as mutations need
independent evaluation.

multiple mutations; allowing us, for the first time, to evaluate and compare
fuzzers with mutation analysis. We introduce an evaluation bench for fuzzers
and apply it to a number of popular fuzzers and subjects. In a comprehensive
evaluation, we show how it allows us to assess fuzzer performance and measure
the impact of improved techniques. While we find that today's fuzzers can
detect only a small percentage of mutations, this should be seen as a challenge
for future research -- notably in improving (1) detecting failures beyond
generic crashes (2) triggering mutations (and thus faults).

allows us to measure the benefit of individual techniques. We find that both
optimizing the fuzzer under test and improving the evaluation technique
lead better mutation detection and thus better fuzzer performance.

us to compare fuzzers independent of the specific subject and fuzzer technology
used.

and Shmaya introduced the class of
$\lambda$-Lipschitz games in which every player's payoff function is
$\lambda$-Lipschitz with respect to the actions of the other players. They
showed that such games admit $\epsilon$-approximate pure Nash equilibria for
certain settings of $\epsilon$ and $\lambda$. They left open, however, the
question of how hard it is to find such an equilibrium. In this work, we
develop a query-efficient reduction from more general games to Lipschitz games.
We use this reduction to show a query lower bound for any randomized algorithm
finding $\epsilon$-approximate pure Nash equilibria of $n$-player,
binary-action, $\lambda$-Lipschitz games that is exponential in
$\frac{n\lambda}{\epsilon}$. In addition, we introduce ``Multi-Lipschitz
games,'' a generalization involving player-specific Lipschitz values, and
provide a reduction from finding equilibria of these games to finding
equilibria of Lipschitz games, showing that the value of interest is the sum of
the individual Lipschitz parameters. Finally, we provide an exponential lower
bound on the deterministic query complexity of finding $\epsilon$-approximate
correlated equilibria of $n$-player, $m$-action, $\lambda$-Lipschitz games,
valid for all $\lambda > \frac{\epsilon}{2}$.

learning, and propose a natural generalization of the reduction to generate
approximate correlated equilibria, which is relevant to the BEAlgorithm of
Daskalas et al.\ [ICALP, 2021]. We show a lower bound on the query complexity
of their algorithm when finding correlated equilibria in Lipschitz games.
Finally, we discuss some interesting questions regarding the relationship
between the query complexity of finding approximate equilibria in Lipschitz
games and recent general lower bound results on the query complexity of
randomized algorithms.

a popular method for estimating the true
performance of machine learning models, allowing model selection and parameter
tuning. However, the very process of CV requires random partitioning of the
data and so our performance estimates are in fact stochastic, with variability
that can be substantial for natural language processing tasks. We demonstrate
that these unstable estimates cannot be relied upon for effective parameter
tuning. The resulting tuned parameters are highly sensitive to how our data is
partitioned, meaning that we often select sub-optimal parameter choices and
have serious reproducibility issues.
  Instead, we propose to use the less variable J-K-fold CV, in which J
independent K-fold cross validations are used to assess performance. Our main
contributions are extending J-K-fold CV from performance estimation to
parameter tuning and investigating how to choose J and K. We argue that
variability is more important than bias for effective tuning and so advocate
lower choices of K than are typically seen in the NLP literature, instead use
the saved computation to increase J. To demonstrate the generality of our
recommendations we investigate a wide range of case-studies: sentiment
classification (both general and target-specific), part-of-speech tagging and
document classification.
  We show that by increasing J (often 10-fold or more) and decreasing K (to
say 5 or 10) we get stable performance estimates and can effectively find the
optimal parameters. We also find that the cost of implementing J-K-fold CV
increases very slowly, meaning that in comparison to other methods we get a
high benefit-to-cost ratio.

introduce the knowledge construction and optimization process during the

directions of knowledge learning are investigated on the Teacher-Student
architecture design, the quality of knowledge, and the theoretical studies of
regression-based learning, respectively. With this comprehensive survey, both

circuit (IC) design. We divide the LBDD problem into five sub-problems:
gatesnet (GN), netlist quality distance learning (L1), netlist quality metric
learning (L2), optimization learning (L3), and architecture evaluation (L4).

netsys (system-level) and nandgraph (gate-level) representations into unique

complexity, and performance. We present various learning technologies for IC

monochromatic light at 689~nm through an ultracold $^{88}$Sr gas, where the
recoil frequency is comparable to natural linewidth of the narrow-line
transition $5\mathrm{s^2}\, ^1\textrm{S}_0 - 5\mathrm{s}5\mathrm{p}\,
^3\textrm{P}_1$ in strontium. In the regime of high-saturation, the absorption
profile becomes asymmetric due to the photon-recoil shift, which is of the same
order as the natural linewidth. The lineshape is described by an extension of
the optical Bloch equations including the momentum transfers to atoms during
emission and absorption of photons. Our work reveals the photon recoil effects
in a simplest single-beam absorption setting, which is of significant relevance
to other applications such as saturation spectroscopy, Ramsey interferometry,
and absorption imaging.
  We also quantify the average momentum changes of atoms in each light-trip or
absorption cycle. This is achieved by measuring the atomic motion induced by a
single light pulse at low temperatures where the thermal phase modulation is
negligible. The average momentum values are in agreement with the classical
estimate within a few percent.
  In an additional experiment, we observe the photon recoil effects become
larger when the laser frequency is detuned from the linear intersection with
the cooling transition. This is because the polarization dependence of the
transition probability introduces an anisotropy of the scattering length,
which enhances the photon recoil effects significantly. The lineshapes can be
fit by the extended optical Bloch equations, which demonstrates that the
formalism can describe the photon recoil effects faithfully in a wide range
of parameters.
  In a different context, the photon recoil effects may play a major role in
recently-proposed schemes of synergetic atom-light interactions, where the
absorption or emission processes are initiated by a perturbing light, and
subsequent internal state changes are driven by another light with a large
recoil frequency.
  In summary, we have observed the photon recoil effects in the absorption of
a single monochromatic light, and the formalism of extended optical Bloch
equations can describe the lineshapes correctly in a wide range of parameters.
This work paves the way for further investigations of the photon recoil
effects in various atom-light interactions.

antiferromagnet provide a promising avenue to realize magnetic analogs of
twisted superfluid and supersolid phases that were recently reported for
two-component ultracold atomic condensate in an optical lattice. Using a
cluster Gutzwiller mean-field theory, we establish that Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya
interactions (DMI), that are common in many quantum magnets, stabilize these
phases in a magnetic system, in contrast to the pair hopping process that is
necessary for ultracold atoms. The critical value of DMI for transition to the
twisted superfluid and twisted supersolid phases depends on the strength of the
(frustrated) interlayer interactions that can be tuned by applying external
pressure on and / or shearing force between the layers. Furthermore, we show
that the strength of DMI can be controllably varied by coupling to tailored
circularly polarized light. Our results provide crucial guidance for the
experimental search of twisted superfluid and supersolid phases of triplons in
real quantum magnets.
  We also show that the strength of DMI can be controlled by coupling the
magnetic material to circularly polarized light. The photoinduced tuning of the
twisted superfluid and twisted supersolid phases is particularly promising for
materials with transition between high-temperature antiferromagnetic and
low-temperature N\'{e}el phases, for which the low-energy magnetic excitations can
be separated from other electromagnetic responses. In such materials, for a
typical experimental error in the temperature measurement, the transition to the
twisted superfluid and twisted supersolid phases can be induced by varying the
frequency of applied light. We illustrate our results using a generic bilayer
antiferromagnet model, but our findings are likely to be common in many
quantum magnets, and thus the experimental evidence of twisted superfluid and
twisted supersolid phases in one material should be considered as strong evidence
for the existence of these phases in other materials.
  The theoretical tools developed in this work can be applied to other multi
layer or solid materials to identify the effect of interlayer interactions on
superfluid and supersolid phases. It would be particularly interesting to
investigate the effect of DMI on superfluid and supersolid phases of two
spins coupled by pair hopping process in a single layer condensate.

the recoil flux of WIMP-scattered target nuclei and on that of the WIMP
effective scattering velocity distribution, we investigate the scattering
probability distribution of the WIMP incident velocity versus the nuclear
recoil angle in narrow recoil energy windows for different WIMP masses and
target nuclei. Our simulation results show that, not only the velocity
distribution of incident halo WIMPs, but also a factor of the recoil angle
could affect the scattering probability distribution of the available incident
velocity-recoil angle combination in a given recoil energy window.
Consequently, the 1-D WIMP "effective" velocity distribution corresponding to
the considered narrow energy window would not be consistent with that cut
simply from the (generating) velocity distribution of incident halo WIMPs. And
its contribution to the differential WIMP-nucleus scattering event rate in the
considered energy window could thus not be simply estimated by integrating over
the 1-D theoretical velocity distribution (of entire halo WIMPs).
  Therefore, to accurately judge the viability of a proposed WIMP search
experiment and to finally determine the correct nucleon capture rate from direct
dark matter experiments, the contributions from the 1-D "effective" velocity
distribution in each considered energy window should not be neglected. In addition, for
different target nuclei, the "effective" velocity distribution would differ due
to a different nuclear recoil angle distribution of WIMP nucleus scattering.
Moreover, due to the different velocity dependencies of the relevant theoretical
capture rate formulas and different "effective" velocity distributions, the
contributions from the 1-D "effective" velocity distribution would be more
important for determining the correct capture rate for some direct detection
experiments.
  In this paper, for the direct WIMP-nucleus scattering experiments and the
related dark matter nucleus recoil experiment EDELWEISS, we will investigate
the scattering probability distribution of the available WIMP incidence velocity-recoil angle combination and its impact on the 1-D "effective" velocity distribution in narrow recoil energy windows for different WIMP masses and target nuclei. The relevant parameters of the "effective" velocity distribution, such as the location of the peak and the width, will be analyzed. In addition, the contributions from the 1-D "effective" velocity distribution to the differential WIMP-nucleus event rate in each considered energy window will be investigated. professional knowledge work is
an understudied area. Here we investigate how public sector officials
self-assess their dependency on the Google Web search engine, whether they are
aware of the potential impact of algorithmic biases on their ability to
retrieve all relevant information, and how much relevant information may
actually be missed due to Web search personalisation. We find that the majority
of participants in our experimental study are neither aware that there is a
potential problem nor do they have a strategy to mitigate the risk of missing
relevant information when performing online searches. Most significantly, we
provide empirical evidence that up to 20% of relevant information may be missed
due to Web search personalisation. This work has significant implications for
Web research by public sector professionals, who should be provided with
training about the potential algorithmic biases that may affect their judgments
and decision making, as well as clear guidelines how to minimise the risk of
missing relevant information.
  We propose a new statistical model to measure the percentage of relevant
information that is not returned due to Web search personalisation. We call this
the Search Dissatisfaction Ratio. We describe how Search Dissatisfaction Ratios
can be measured via simple human evaluation tasks that be performed on a
sample of search results. We demonstrate our approach on 1,582 search terms
related to climate change. We find that up to 20% of relevant information may
be missed due to Web search personalisation, and that Search Dissatisfaction
Ratios can vary significantly based on search terms. We release our dataset of
search terms to facilitate further research on algorithmic biases in Web
search personalisation.
  Web search engines are critical tools for many professionals including journalists
and public sector officials who require accurate and reliable information to
perform their work. Personalisation can lead to content biases in search
results that may reflect the social biases of the population a model is

people demonstrated significant gender and racial biases that were correlated
with search rankings. Here, we investigate search content biases in a
general-search engine, namely Google Web search, and a knowledge graph-specific
search engine, Wikipedia, using a diverse topic dataset of 1,582 topics. We
find that both Google and Wikipedia searches are biased towards topics related

facility at the TeV scale that is capable of performing precision deep
inelastic scattering measurements in new regimes and providing a rich program
in nuclear and particle physics. Such a facility could seed, or leverage, the
development of a muon-antimuon collider and make use of the existing hadron
accelerator infrastructure when sited at a facility such as Brookhaven National
Laboratory, Fermilab, or CERN. We discuss the possible energy and luminosity
design parameters for several collider configurations, and illustrate the

  From Oct. 2019 to Apr.2020, a pandemic-led experiment was conducted to
understand the behavior of large crowds at a supermarket in Australia. A
supermarket was divided into 7 sectors, and 2000 citizens were asked to visit
the supermarket according to one of 7000 different trial schedules. The
experimental design and analysis are presented to show how randomization and
control allow for the estimation of the infection risk of interacting with
other people in the supermarket, and how this design can be extended to
investigate other questions about COVID-19.
  We propose a novel experiment to address the deep learning integrity problem
of "adversarial examples," i.e., situations in which artificial neural networks
make incorrect predictions on visual input intended to represent possible
errors, with a practical application to security screening. The key idea is
to use a large number of untrained humans to classify images that are known to
be incorrect by the network, to estimate the frequency of such images in the
data population. We show that the frequencies of incorrect predictions by the
network are directly proportional to the frequencies of similar errors by
humans, indicating that the main cause of these events is
data-noisyness. We propose a simple algorithm to detect such cases by minimax
game between humans and the network, and vice versa. Our experiments show
that the frequencies of adversarial examples measured by humans are 100x smaller
than those by the network, indicating that most of the adversarial examples
generated by the test set are also noisy, and that the test errors by the
network will significantly improve with data reprocessing.

  Methods: k-space data are continuously acquired using a rewound Cartesian
acquisition with spiral profile ordering (rCASPR) to provide matching contrast
to the conventional linear phase encode ordering and to sort data into multiple
respiratory phases. Low-resolution respiratory-correlated 4D images were
reconstructed with compressed sensing and used to estimate non-rigid
deformation vector fields, which were subsequently used for a motion
compensated image reconstruction. rCASPR sampling was compared to linear and
CASPR sampling in terms of point-spread-function (PSF) and image contrast with
in silico, phantom and in vivo experiments. Reconstruction parameters for
low-resolution 4D-MRI (spatial resolution and temporal regularization) were
determined using a grid search. The proposed motion compensated rCASPR was
evaluated in eight healthy volunteers and compared to free-breathing scans with
linear sampling. Image quality was compared based on visual inspection and
quantitatively by means of the gradient entropy.
  Results: rCASPR provided a superior PSF (similar in ky and narrower in kz)
and showed no considerable differences in images contrast compared to linear
sampling. The optimal 4D-MRI reconstruction parameters were a temporal
regularization of 0.06 s$^2$ and a spatial resolution of 2 mm. Volunteering
images reconstructed from the proposed rCASPR protocol showed similar image
quality to 4D-MRI reconstructions with linear sampling, with the advantage of
recreating more homogeneous mr fluid-filled structures such as the spine
cavity and the knee joint. Visual inspection and quantitative results
demonstrated that the gradient entropy and visual inspection indicated
superior image quality for the rCASPR protocol compared to linear sampling,
particularly in the lateral direction.
  Conclusion: The proposed rCASPR protocol shows promise for acquiring
high-contrast 4D $T_2$-weighted images without breath-holding.

a subset of the safe set of states, and constructs a controller to render the
subset forward invariant. The feedback controller is represented as the
solution to a quadratic program, which can be solved efficiently for real-time

  We present a novel framework to address safety-critical control tasks that
require human intervention. Human operators often insert themselves into the
automation loop to fix safety-critical situations in autonomous systems.
Identifying these situations promptly and efficiently controlling the system
while re-establishing safety is crucial. We pose the solution as a partially
ordered goal-based task and present a computational framework that combines
artificial intelligence and computer science techniques. We leverage goal-based
control to define a set of goals that encompass the safety requirements and
range of possible situations. A set of strategies, representing ways to achieve
these goals, are parameterized and organized hierarchically in a control
hierarchy. A set of modes, representing specific combinations of installed
strategies, are defined to address specific situations. At runtime, the
reconfigurable control hierarchy is used to activate the appropriate mode,
which includes the suitable installed strategies. We define a set of conditions
for detection and insertion into the automation loop, and we use observation
methods to trigger the modes. We use goal satisfaction methods to activate the
strategies of a mode and to check for goal satisfaction. Finally, we use
reconfigurability methods to update the control hierarchy and to change the
installed strategies and modes. We present a naval vessel case study to
demonstrate the effectiveness of our framework.

suitable family endowed with set-inclusion order of some mathematical
structures. In this paper, representations of domains via CF-approximation
spaces are considered. Concepts of CF-approximation spaces and CF-closed sets
are introduced. It is proved that the family of CF-closed sets in a
CF-approximation space endowed with set-inclusion order is a continuous domain
and that every continuous domain is isomorphic to the family of CF-closed sets
of some CF-approximation space endowed with set-inclusion order. The concept of
CF-approximable relations is introduced using a categorical approach, which
later facilitates the proof that the category of CF-approximation spaces and
CF-approximable relations is equivalent to that of continuous domains and Scott
continuous maps.
  As an application, a decision problem in CF-approximation spaces is
introduced and a solution based on a correspondence with a given constraint
satisfaction problem is given. The solution does not rely on the approximation
property of CF-approximation spaces and the concept of CF-closed sets is not
needed for its derivation. Nevertheless, the underlying representation of a
domain by a CF-approximation space is crucial for transferring properties from
the domain to the CF-approximation space and back, in order to solve the
problem.
  Finally, a comparison with other representations of domains is given. A
brief overview of other representations of domains is provided and the main
difficulties in comparing them is discussed. A solution to a problem
considering relational databases and information systems, which is similar to
the decision problem considered in this paper, is presented. The main
difference is that it relies on the information system part of CF-approximation
spaces. The solution does not rely on the approximation property, but again,
the underlying representation of a domain is crucial for transferring
properties from the domain to the information system and back, in order to
solve the problem.

a vital role in developing NLP systems to provide confidence that the
difference in performance between two systems (i.e., the test statistic) is not
due to luck. However, practitioners rely on Monte Carlo approximation to
perform this test due to a lack of a suitable exact algorithm. In this paper,
we provide an efficient exact algorithm for the paired-permutation test for a
family of structured test statistics. Our algorithm runs in $\mathcal{O}(GN
(\log GN )(\log N ))$ time where $N$ is the dataset size and $G$ is the range
of the test statistic. We found that our exact algorithm was $10$x faster than
the Monte Carlo approximation with $20000$ samples on a common dataset.
Moreover, we find that the discrepancy between exact and approximate results
grows with the difference in performance; hence, our exact algorithm is particularly
important for fairness debiasing techniques that aim to remove bias away from
the average performance.
  We also develop a semiexact algorithm that is 4x faster than the current
state-of-the-art exact algorithm. While the speedup is not significant for
current datasets, our approach can be used as a starting point for developing
faster algorithms. Most importantly, our studies highlight the importance of
exact solution for significance testing in developing NLP systems.
  We further investigate the impact of the approximate nature of the Monte
Carry library (the most widely used library for exact permutation test) in
two recent fairness de-biasing papers. We demonstrate that, for the
datasets considered in those papers, the Monte Carry library is accurate
beyond $4$ digits for all test statistics of interest.
  We also investigate the role of significance testing in two recent NLP
papers: mean average precision based ranking task and multi-task learning. We
demonstrate that the usual practice of rounding the p-value to $0.05$ may not
lead to the desired result; hence, we propose an alternative approach to
ensure at least one system is significantly better than a baseline.
  Finally, we highlight the need for a closed-loop system between algorithm
design and the use of exact algorithm for significance testing. Currently,
algorithm developers do not know which systems to compute the exact p-value for
because there is no framework to connect the performance difference to the
computational resources required for the exact test.

among the six cartels. We estimate the model for two time periods: before and

two - Far East - Far West and Far East - Far East - are in the second period.
Also, the sensitivity of prices to quantities is much stronger in the first
than in the second period, suggesting that the cartels may have charged
different prices at different levels of industry quantity in the first period.
Finally, we find strong evidence of competition among cartels in terms of
prices and quantities.
